Theorem 3 denominators contain omega_t^(j) inside sums indexed by l, in both equations (3.8a/b). Theorem 6 repeats this in (3.19). Theorem 5 instead uses omega_t^(l) in (3.15). Images confirm these are source indices, not extraction artifacts.

Theorem 6 defines its measure with equal weights 1/m, while its ODE contains omega_t^(j) without dynamics or an explicit value there. Retain this unresolved source meaning; do not silently insert 1/m into the ODE.

The simplex permits zero weights, which make the printed j-indexed denominators in Theorem 3 zero for a zero-weight particle. With nonuniform weights, the displayed dynamics also have unresolved mass-preservation/PDE consistency. Source review is not proof certification.

Uniform sampling from {X_i} may mean the empirical multiset versus distinct locations if observations repeat. Initial locations are random in T3/T6, but arbitrary fixed locations are introduced before T5; do not add random initialization to T5.

Pushforward is stated for any mapping, without an explicit measurability condition. The distributional-solution convention only uses spatial test functions and a time derivative; temporal regularity and pointwise/a.e. time scope are unstated.

Theorem 2 uses measure update (3.7): Fisher-Rao weight update first, then Wasserstein pushforward of the intermediate measure. Algorithm 1 reverses location/weight order and also uses j-indexed denominators. It must not be substituted for (3.7).
Gradient-flow PDEs use the fixed representative delta ell_N with a particular additive constant. Preserve the explicit formulas, not a generic first-variation-up-to-constant replacement.

Main-text pages 4–5 describe centered reaction action, Wasserstein action/couplings and WFR action. Review endpoint/admissibility conventions and the apparent centered-Fisher-Rao versus Hellinger closed-form mismatch without consulting appendices.
